# Rule 9 — Antagonist expectations
Antagonists are allowed to create conflict, danger, and chaos, but they are still expected to roleplay and create an enjoyable round.
Your objectives give you permission to pursue antagonist actions, but they do not require you to ignore roleplay, rush murder, or destroy the entire round without interaction.
Escalation still matters. Give players a chance to notice, respond, negotiate, investigate, or fight back when reasonable.
Avoid unnecessary mass destruction unless your antagonist role, objectives, or the current roleplay situation clearly supports it. The goal is to create a memorable story, not simply to end the round as fast as possible.
Antagonists may lie, steal, sabotage, kidnap, injure, or kill when it fits their role and objectives, but they should avoid targeting the same player repeatedly without reason or ruining unrelated players’ rounds for no purpose.
